prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: defer_sign_in_after_adoption [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +12.0%, measured -7.7% ± 2.1%, after noise correction -5.2%, stopped early: sign_in worse
- round 1: interactive_wait_minigame [home, new_flow]: predicted +8.0%, measured +2.9% ± 2.0%, after noise correction +2.1%, lost: no clear effect
- round 1: custom_photo_guidelines [adoption, copy]: predicted +11.0%, measured -0.6% ± 2.8%, after noise correction -0.3%, lost: no clear effect
- round 1: desktop_pet_summon_shortcut_banner [finish, notification]: predicted +7.0%, measured -0.8% ± 3.6%, after noise correction -0.3%, lost: no clear effect

By kind of change, after noise correction:
- adoption, copy: -0.3% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, notification: -0.3% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, new_flow: +2.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: -5.2% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

One test is weak evidence. State a rule only when at least 2 tests of that kind agree after noise correction; otherwise say the evidence is still thin.

Previous lessons:
(none yet)

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Evidence is still thin for all change types (sign_in reorder, home new_flow, adoption copy, finish notification) since each has only been tested once.
Reordering sign-in performed poorly (-5.2% after noise correction) and was stopped early, but evidence is still thin to form a permanent rule.
No clear effect was seen for home new_flow, adoption copy, or finish notification changes.
Predictions were consistently too high compared to measured and noise-corrected results across all tests.
